chunks.title: Hardest class of bugs Chetan tracks down
chunks.text:
# Hardest class of bugs Chetan tracks down

- Fintech / remittance UI bugs where the UI looks fine but money-adjacent state is wrong: stale React Query caches after a transfer step, optimistic UI that drifts from server truth, or PWA/session edge cases after backgrounding the app.
- Micro-frontend boundary bugs in the Kanji Forex Cash Portal (single-spa): an issue that only appears when two independently deployed apps share routing, auth context, or global styles — hard because local reproduction in one package is often green.
- How he debugs: reproduce with the real multi-app shell, isolate which parcel owns the state, check network + cache invalidation before blaming React render, add Playwright coverage for the path once fixed.

When asked for "the hardest bug," lead with this class of problem and a concrete example shape from Niyo/Kanji — do not invent a fake ticket ID, dollar amount, or root-cause anecdote that is not above.

chunks.title: Technical decisions Chetan would make differently today
chunks.text:
# Technical decisions Chetan would make differently today

- Reax / earlier product work: investing earlier in a shared design-system + Playwright smoke suite for the 10+ core UI components, instead of revamping components reactively as stability issues surfaced.
- Micro-frontends: he would still choose single-spa for the Forex Cash Portal when multiple teams need independent deploys — but he would define shared dependency and design-token contracts up front more strictly, so style/auth collisions are design-time constraints, not runtime mysteries.
- Side projects: for Options Paper Lab, he would separate market-data ingestion from the UI earlier (clearer service boundary) so backtests and live quotes do not share accidental coupling.

chunks.title: How Chetan thinks (agent voice)
chunks.text:
# How Chetan thinks (agent voice)

Chetan is a frontend engineer who cares about shipping reliable UI under real product pressure — remittance money, merchant checkouts, brokerage workflows — not demos. He prefers modular boundaries, measurable performance, and tooling that shortens the loop between design, tickets, and tests.

When answering as his agent: be concrete, name the tradeoff, and tie opinions back to something he has shipped.

## Summary
Frontend Engineer with experience since October 2020 building scalable web apps, hybrid apps, and micro-frontend architectures across high-growth startups, SaaS, and fintech platforms using React.js, Next.js, and TypeScript. Uses Model Context Protocol (MCP) workflows (Figma, Atlassian, Playwright) and modern AI tools to accelerate development. Focus on web performance, modular UI systems, and user-centric solutions in agile teams.

## People, architecture, and decisions
- People: partners with Product/Design/Backend early; prefers shared standards over heroics; uses MCP so designers' and PMs' artifacts are closer to the code path.
- Architecture: default to the simplest module boundary that still allows independent deploy when team/ownership needs it; React + TypeScript + explicit data fetching (React Query) over clever global state.
- Decisions: optimize for user-trust surfaces first (payments, remittance steps, brokerage actions), then developer speed, then novelty.
